Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple, bilateral, peripheral nodular opacities (indicated by arrows), some of which appear to have central lucency or cavitation. This pattern of multifocal, wedge-shaped, or rounded peripheral lesions is the classic radiological presentation of septic pulmonary emboli, typically arising from a source like tricuspid valve endocarditis. While cavitating metastases can look similar, the acute inflammatory appearance and distribution strongly favor septic emboli in this context.
